## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Adhikaraṇavāra* is the sixth section of the opening division of the *Parivāra*, the closing procedural and analytical compendium of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In keeping with the analytical format of this portion of the *Parivāra*, the chapter systematically relates the various Vinaya rules to the four recognized classes of legal issues or procedures (*adhikaraṇa*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translation of the text has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali, alongside other translations recorded by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in non-Pali corpora are recorded by SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal text reuse comprising 73 matching passages across 19 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur within the *Parivāra* itself, notably with corresponding *Adhikaraṇavāra* chapters (Pvr 2.6, Pvr 2.14, and Pvr 1.14) and other catechistic analyses of offenses such as the *Samuṭṭhānavāra* (Pvr 1.5, Pvr 1.13), *Samathavāra* (Pvr 1.7, Pvr 1.15), *Saṅgahitavāra* (Pvr 1.4, Pvr 1.12), *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 1.3, Pvr 1.11), *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 1.8), and *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5) [DharmaNexus]. Portions of its phrasing also recur in post-canonical Vinaya subcommentarial treatises, specifically the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā* and the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
